chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: When you place your forehead on a raised spot, do not lift it; rather, drag it onto the ground.

key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the ground, the proper surface to which the forehead should be moved in prostration
key_terms.جَبْهَتَكَ: your forehead, the part placed on the ground in sajdah
key_terms.جُرَّهَا: drag it, meaning move the forehead along without lifting
key_terms.فَلَا تَرْفَعْهَا: do not lift it, meaning do not raise the forehead after it has been placed down
key_terms.نَبَكَةٍ: a raised spot or elevated mound on the place of prostration

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in sajdah if his forehead falls on a raised place?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sajdah in salat. If a person's forehead lands on an elevated place during prostration, he should not raise it up and repeat the motion, but instead move it along to the ground, preserving the correctness of the act.
